name: Shahid Malik
citation: CNN, 'British expenses scandal claims justice minister' (cnn.com/2009/WORLD/europe/05/15/uk.mps.expenses.malik); UK Parliament members' career record (members.parliament.uk/member/1509/career) for the exact end date
source_note: Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Justice, stepped down 15 May 2009 pending an inquiry into his own expenses claims (GBP66,827 second-home allowance while paying below-market rent at his registered main home) - reported as 'the first government member forced out by the expenses scandal.' Found via the 10 Sep 2026 sweep (Wikipedia per-government departure pages + targeted search), not the original opportunistic pass. Later cleared by the inquiry, but the DEPARTURE event itself is what BDD's own method counts, regardless of eventual exoneration (same logic as their Mellor/Fairbairn treatment).

name: Kitty Ussher
citation: France 24, 'Expenses scandal claims new victim' (france24.com/en/20090618-expenses-scandal-claims-new-victim-); Wikipedia, 'Kitty Ussher' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Ussher) for the exact date and post
source_note: Exchequer Secretary to the Treasury, resigned 17 June 2009 - hours before a Telegraph story broke on her having temporarily redesignated her Burnley home as a 'second home' to avoid up to GBP17,000 in capital gains tax on its sale. Only 8 days into the post (appointed in the 9 June reshuffle). Checked against this project's own IfG appointment.csv: only 2 appointment-endings on 2009-06-17 (well below the 5+ reshuffle-cluster threshold) - genuinely standalone, NOT reshuffle-clustered like Blears/McNulty (5 June), so included on the same principled basis as Malik. Found via the 10 Sep 2026 BBC/open-media search pass, not Wikipedia or the original opportunistic pass.
